curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `H M L`; `zt zz zb`; `Ctrl-f`, `Ctrl-b`, `Ctrl-d`, `Ctrl-u`, `Ctrl-e`, `Ctrl-y`; `m{char}`; `'` and backtick jumps; special marks such as `'.`, ```.```, `'^`, ```^```, `'[`, `']`; `Ctrl-o`, `Ctrl-i`; `g;`, `g,`; `gi`, `gv`; advanced bracket/section motions
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Move through a large edit without losing important locations, and return to prior jumps, changes, insertions, or selections
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Inspect a distant definition and return; revisit the last change; center a target line; mark two sites and shuttle between them
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core through marks, jump/change lists, and viewport commands. Code-section motions are advanced and syntax-dependent

lessons.title: Read the visible window
lessons.objective: Use H, M, and L to reach visible window landmarks.

activities.title: Move to the top, middle, or bottom of the window
activities.body: Press `H`, `M`, or `L` to move to the highest, middle, or lowest visible line. These commands use the current window, not fixed file line numbers.
activities.grammar: H -> visible top; M -> visible middle; L -> visible bottom
activities.contrast: Their destinations change when the viewport changes.

lessons.objective: Use representative section, block, and method boundary motions.

activities.title: Move between large code structures
activities.body: Bracket motions can find sections, unmatched brackets, and brace-delimited methods. Use them only when the file has clear matching structure.

lessons.title: Keep your place in a large edit
lessons.objective: Combine marks, viewport movement, and history returns.

activities.title: Choose how you plan to return
activities.body: Use a mark for a place you choose in advance, the jump list for places reached by large moves, the change list for edit locations, and window commands only to change the view.
activities.grammar: planned place -> mark; traveled path -> jump list; edited place -> change list
activities.contrast: The shortest command is not always the clearest recovery strategy.

hints: Choose the history or viewport command that preserves your place.
Use backtick-a backtick-b.

feedback.why: Two named marks make planned sites addressable.

activities.title: Choose the right return path
activities.prompt: After several edits and a distant jump, which command most directly revisits the previous edit?
activities.explanation: g; follows edit positions, including edits that were undone.

activities.title: Navigate without losing context
activities.body: Large-buffer fluency separates viewport framing, planned marks, travel history, edit history, and structural destinations.
takeaways: Use window-relative commands when only the visible frame matters.
Use lowercase marks for planned returns.
Use Ctrl-o/Ctrl-i for jumps and g;/g, for edits.
Use structural motions only with reliable textual boundaries.

reference.purpose: Reach top, middle, or bottom visible rows.

notes: The logical cursor does not move.

reference.command: Ctrl-f Ctrl-b Ctrl-d Ctrl-u Ctrl-e Ctrl-y
reference.purpose: Move by pages, half pages, or viewport rows.

notes: Small local motions do not create the same trail.

reference.purpose: Return to the last change, Insert exit, or Visual selection.
notes: Change and insertion history can differ.

reference.purpose: Reach the boundaries of changed or yanked text.

notes: Comment and preprocessor motions are excluded.
